hints: In $\triangle ADB$, $AD = 5$, $AB = 5 + 8 = 13$, and $\angle ADB = 90^\circ$. Use Pythagoras to find side $BD$.
Since $E$ is on the circle with centre $B$ (radius $8$), the straight segment length $DE = BD - BE = 12 - 8 = 4\text{ cm}$.
Find angle $\angle DAB = \cos^{-1}(5/13)$ and angle $\angle ABD = \sin^{-1}(5/13)$ in radians.
Calculate the lengths of arcs $CD$ and $CE$ using $s = r\theta$, and sum with $DE$ to find the total perimeter.
walkthrough:
Apply Pythagoras' theorem in the right-angled triangle $\triangle ADB$ with hypotenuse $AB = 5 + 8 = 13\text{ cm}$ and side $AD = 5\text{ cm}$:
$$BD = \sqrt{AB^2 - AD^2} = \sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = 12\text{ cm}$$
Since $E$ lies on circle $B$ of radius $8\text{ cm}$, $BE = 8\text{ cm}$, so the segment $DE$ is:
$$DE = BD - BE = 12 - 8 = 4\text{ cm}$$

Calculate angles $\angle DAB$ and $\angle ABD$ in radians:
$$\angle DAB = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) \approx 1.1760\text{ rad}$$
$$\angle ABD = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{13}\right) = \frac{\pi}{2} - 1.1760 \approx 0.3948\text{ rad}$$

Calculate the lengths of arc $CD$ (circle $A$, radius $5$) and arc $CE$ (circle $B$, radius $8$) using $s = r\theta$:
$$s_{CD} = 5 \times 1.1760 = 5.8800\text{ cm}$$
$$s_{CE} = 8 \times 0.3948 = 3.1584\text{ cm}$$

Sum all boundary components to find the total perimeter of the shaded region:
$$\text{Perimeter} = s_{CD} + s_{CE} + DE = 5.8800 + 3.1584 + 4 = 13.0384 \approx 13.0\text{ cm}$$

hints: Calculate the area of right-angled triangle $\triangle ADB$ using $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.
Calculate the area of sector $ACD$ using $\frac{1}{2} r_A^2 \theta_A$ and sector $BCE$ using $\frac{1}{2} r_B^2 \theta_B$.
Subtract both sector areas from the triangle area to obtain the shaded region area.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle $\triangle ADB$:
$$\text{Area}(\triangle ADB) = \frac{1}{2} \times AD \times BD = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 12 = 30\text{ cm}^2$$

Calculate the areas of circular sectors $ACD$ and $BCE$ using $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } ACD) = \frac{1}{2} \times 5^2 \times 1.1760 = 14.700\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Area}(\text{sector } BCE) = \frac{1}{2} \times 8^2 \times 0.3948 = 12.634\text{ cm}^2$$

Subtract the areas of both unshaded sectors from the total triangle area:
$$\text{Area}(\text{shaded}) = 30 - 14.700 - 12.634 = 2.666 \approx 2.67\text{ cm}^2$$
